items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I heard Eddie think I had Eddy Lang, and I made up my mind I was going to play, be a guitarist.

ctx.x: Well, that was from around 12, 13. I was playing, you know, with her band then. And she had let's see one guy I remember particularly, his name was Lorenzo Wardell. He had played with let's see -- was it McKinney's cotton pickers? From Detroit. Yeah, a very fine -- but any way, he played in our band. And another guy who was a trombone player with Benny Carter was also in our band, his name was Alton Moore. And these were real pros. And Montgomery, Handy -- at this time Handy would do tours, also. And he'd bring…

know. These were real stars.
So I had just been engulfed in music, just surrounded by music all my life. Now, how I started playing guitar. I heard Eddie think I had Eddy Lang, and I made up my mind I was going to play, be a guitarist. And I really taught myself, because I would hear certain voicings on a guitar, and I would just fool with it until I got just the voicings I wanted, which was kind of unorthodox. And it took an awful lot of work, I guess it took years and years and years for me to develop, you…

And this is how I started. And my mother also at this time we left -- let's see, we left Montgomery, and we went to Chicago. This was around 1920 something, I was very small, you know. And I went to school in Chicago, and I went to school with Ray Nance. And -- who was a tremendous musician. We were in Wendell Wenda Philipps together. But Wendell Philipps High School. They had a very good band then. Nance had a very good band. I used to play with Nance's band, incidently.
